plan: Store the constructor's dictionary via copy.deepcopy so the workspace owns an isolated tree; to_data() returns another deep copy.

Centralize traversal in a single recursive generator that yields (item, depth) in document order over sections, groups, notes, and references; build word count, marker collection, and outline on top of it.

Compile two module-level regexes: one for marker tokens [[?identifier]] and one for words (\b\w+\b); count note words on text with markers replaced by a space so identifiers never count and adjacent words never merge.
Aggregate unresolved markers from note marker identifiers plus reference 'unresolved' lists into a set, returned sorted lexicographically.
Render outline as the workspace title followed by one line per item: two spaces per nesting level (top-level items at level 1) plus '<kind>: <title>'.

Implement move with a locate helper returning (parent list, index, item); validate everything before mutating: string ids, existence, container destination ('workspace' literal maps to the root list), cycle check via identity search of the destination inside the moved subtree, and insertion index bounds 0..len(destination); only then pop from the source list and append/insert into the destination, which makes failed moves trivially side-effect free.
Keep everything standard-library-only (copy, re) so in-memory tests need no fixtures.
mechanisms: Deep-copy ownership boundary at construction and export (copy.deepcopy)
Single document-order (item, depth) generator shared by all read operations
Precompiled marker/word regexes with marker-stripping before word counting
Set-based marker aggregation with sorted output
Depth-indexed outline formatting (two spaces per level)
Validate-then-mutate move protocol guaranteeing atomicity on failure
Identity-based subtree containment check to reject self/descendant moves
